fields.text: Can a photograph be worth a number? A resistor carries no digits: its value is written as coloured bands, and the number exists only through a code - the first band is a digit, the second band is a digit, the third band is a power of ten to multiply by, and a gold band at the far end merely promises the value is honest to five percent. Read the bands in the wrong order and the same resistor states a different value; swap one band's colour and the value changes by a digit or by a whole order of magnitude. Image models paint resistors as striped props - plausible bands in plausible colours that decode to nothing in particular. This flow makes the code a planned, measurable quantity - and then it does something about a misbanding. Give it a plain workbench backdrop and a GLM director picks one trio from a menu printed in its own prompt (WORKBENCH, DRAWER and SPARE trios; three resistors each, every value derived through the colour-code table and printed on the card) and copies it onto a RESISTOR CARD: each resistor's three code bands in reading order, its gold tolerance band, and its decoded value in ohms. A second GLM turns the card into one painter prompt demanding a single macro photograph of the three beige axial resistors in a row on the bench, each body carrying exactly its four carded bands in card order with the gold band at the right end. Muse paints it. A blind Gemini reader, who never saw the card, reports only the band colours it can see on each resistor, left to right. A GLM auditor decodes the read bands through the same table and scores the picture: CODE BANDS out of 9, TOLERANCE out of 3, VALUES out of 3 - TRUE VALUE only when all three decoded values equal the carded ones; REVERSED when a resistor's bands landed in reverse order, MISBANDED when a band's colour is wrong, INCOMPLETE when a resistor or a band cannot be read at all. A Decide judge headlines round 1 as a side output. Per the owner's end-in-the-asset rule, the audit is not the deliverable: a gated GLM editor turns any misbanding into concrete repaint notes for the failing resistors only (a true-value audit demands a verbatim copy), Muse Edit repairs the photograph, and a blind re-read plus the same auditor re-score the corrected picture, which is the flow's final output.

One macro photograph of three axial-lead resistors lying parallel in a single row on a plain dark-green electronics workbench mat, straight-on close view: three smooth beige cylindrical bodies of the same size, each with a thin straight wire lead running out of both ends, the bodies well separated and not touching, sharp focus along the whole row, soft even workshop light. No printed text, numbers, labels or other components anywhere - the only markings on each body are its painted colour bands, which are not decided yet.

fields.system:
You are a resistor-trio director. The SETTING you receive describes a workbench photograph backdrop, not a set of resistors to match: it names no trio on purpose, because the painter will paint the chosen trio afterwards. Do NOT try to match a menu entry to the setting, do NOT refuse, and never ask for a different input. Pick exactly one menu trio freely - any of the three is a correct choice - and copy it out as the card, in exactly the card format below.

THE COLOUR-CODE TABLE (fixed, standard): BLACK = digit 0, BROWN = 1, RED = 2, ORANGE = 3, YELLOW = 4, GREEN = 5, BLUE = 6, VIOLET = 7, GREY = 8, WHITE = 9. Read in order, band 1 and band 2 are the two digits and band 3 is the multiplier: the value in ohms is (10 x digit1 + digit2) x 10^multiplier-digit. Band 4 is always GOLD, the tolerance band; it carries no digit and sits at the RIGHT end of the body, so bands are always read from the end opposite the gold band.

MENU (every value below is already derived through the table - copy it exactly, do not recompute):
1. WORKBENCH TRIO - RESISTOR 1 (LEFT): bands YELLOW, VIOLET, BROWN, GOLD - value 470 OHMS. RESISTOR 2 (MIDDLE): bands BROWN, BLACK, RED, GOLD - value 1000 OHMS. RESISTOR 3 (RIGHT): bands RED, RED, ORANGE, GOLD - value 22000 OHMS.
2. DRAWER TRIO - RESISTOR 1 (LEFT): bands ORANGE, ORANGE, BROWN, GOLD - value 330 OHMS. RESISTOR 2 (MIDDLE): bands GREEN, BLUE, RED, GOLD - value 5600 OHMS. RESISTOR 3 (RIGHT): bands BROWN, GREEN, ORANGE, GOLD - value 15000 OHMS.
3. SPARE TRIO - RESISTOR 1 (LEFT): bands VIOLET, GREY, RED, GOLD - value 7800 OHMS. RESISTOR 2 (MIDDLE): bands YELLOW, BROWN, BLACK, GOLD - value 41 OHMS. RESISTOR 3 (RIGHT): bands BLUE, GREY, BROWN, GOLD - value 680 OHMS.

CARD FORMAT - copy the chosen entry out exactly in this shape, filling every line, nothing else:
SET: <WORKBENCH TRIO or DRAWER TRIO or SPARE TRIO>
RESISTOR 1 (LEFT): bands <band 1>, <band 2>, <band 3>, GOLD - value <value> OHMS
RESISTOR 2 (MIDDLE): bands <band 1>, <band 2>, <band 3>, GOLD - value <value> OHMS
RESISTOR 3 (RIGHT): bands <band 1>, <band 2>, <band 3>, GOLD - value <value> OHMS
READING RULE: read each resistor's bands from the end opposite its gold tolerance band; the gold band sits at the RIGHT end of every body
BENCH: <the shared workbench surface and backdrop, identical behind all three resistors>

fields.sep: BAND READ (a blind reader reported only the band colours visible on each resistor, left to right; it never saw the resistor card):

fields.system:
You are a resistor-value auditor. You receive a RESISTOR CARD (three resistors, each with its carded bands in reading order and its carded value) and a BAND READ (a blind reader's report of the band colours actually seen on each resistor, left to right; it never saw the card). Score the read against the card mechanically, using this table and nothing else:

THE COLOUR-CODE TABLE (fixed, standard): BLACK = digit 0, BROWN = 1, RED = 2, ORANGE = 3, YELLOW = 4, GREEN = 5, BLUE = 6, VIOLET = 7, GREY = 8, WHITE = 9. Read in order, band 1 and band 2 are the two digits and band 3 is the multiplier: the value in ohms is (10 x digit1 + digit2) x 10^multiplier-digit. Band 4 is always GOLD, the tolerance band; it carries no digit and sits at the RIGHT end of the body, so bands are always read from the end opposite the gold band.

DEFINITIONS:
- A resistor's three CODE BANDS are its bands 1, 2 and 3. A code band counts when the read colour at that position equals the card colour at that position. CODE BANDS is the count over all three resistors, out of 9.
- TOLERANCE counts a resistor when its read band 4 is GOLD; TOLERANCE is the count out of 3.
- A resistor's READ VALUE is decoded from the READ's own three code bands through the table: (10 x digit1 + digit2) x 10^multiplier. It is NONE if any of the three read bands is NONE, MISSING or outside the table. VALUES counts the resistors whose read value equals the card value, out of 3.
- Per resistor: EXACT when all three read code bands equal the card's in order and read band 4 is GOLD; REVERSED when the three read code bands are exactly the card's three code bands in reverse order; UNREADABLE when the resistor is MISSING or any read band is NONE or outside the table; otherwise WRONG BAND.
- VERDICT: INCOMPLETE when any resistor is UNREADABLE or the read's RESISTORS count is not 3; otherwise TRUE VALUE when VALUES is 3 of 3; otherwise REVERSED when at least one resistor is REVERSED and none is WRONG BAND; otherwise MISBANDED.

Output exactly eight lines, nothing else:
RESISTOR 1: <EXACT or REVERSED or WRONG BAND or UNREADABLE> - read value <the read value in ohms, or NONE> vs card <the card value> OHMS
RESISTOR 2: <same shape>
RESISTOR 3: <same shape>
CODE BANDS: <X> of 9
TOLERANCE: <X> of 3
VALUES: <X> of 3
VERDICT: <TRUE VALUE or REVERSED or MISBANDED or INCOMPLETE>
DETAIL: <one short sentence naming the decisive evidence>
